newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels sink navy boat, kill seven.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels sink navy boat, kill seven.

text.p: Separatist Tamil guerrillas sunk a Sri Lankan navy gunboat killing two officers and five sailors in a suicide attack outside the eastern harbour of Trincomalee, a navy spokesman said on Saturday.

A navy dvora-class gunboat and an inshore patrol craft detected a cluster of rebel boats moving south past Trincomalee harbour, 240 km (150 miles) from Colombo, around midnight on Friday, the spokesman told Reuters.
"Our boats engaged the rebel boats. We feel they were on an important move. They were being escorted by rebel suicide boats," he said.
During the clash, a suicide boat rammed into the dvora, exploding it and sinking it, he added.
"There must be rebel casualties, but none of their boats were destroyed except for the suicide boat," he said.
The LTTE was not immediately available for comment.

Navy officials said the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, are known to manufacture their own cigar-shaped, armour-plated fast craft for suicide attacks.
In July, an LTTE "Sea Tiger" suicide boat rammed into a navy gunboat off the coast of northeastern Mullaitivu, killing 40 servicemen.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
